summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore and EBITDA to INR89.7 crore after the Bhopal licence suspension; FY27 guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore, EBITDA declined to INR89.7 crore and PAT was INR10.2 crore. Beer volumes dropped 20% to 187.19 lakh cases, driven by the temporary licence suspension at the Bhopal plant and weak demand in Karnataka and Odisha, while IMFL grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases. Management said the Bhopal licence renewal is pending with authorities, with no definite timeline; the UP greenfield brewery has begun trials and commercial production is expected from June 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR1,400-1,500 crore and FY27 EBITDA margin to close to 10%, with FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

segments.name: Beer
segments.commentary: Volumes fell 20% to 187.19 lakh cases in FY26 due to the Bhopal licence disruption and weak Karnataka and Odisha demand. Management said Karnataka is improving after excise rationalisation, and April-May industry growth was about 15-16%.

segments.name: IMFL / premium spirits
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases in FY26, led by premium portfolio penetration. Mahavat Whisky was launched in the mid-premium segment, and supply was halted when Bhopal stopped.

segments.name: Bhopal plant
segments.commentary: Management said roughly 50% of company volume historically came from Bhopal. Production has been halted since February and Delhi, UP and Jharkhand supplies from this plant stopped; finished goods were cleared and sold.

segments.name: UP greenfield brewery (subsidiary SDBL)
segments.commentary: About INR250 crore invested in FY26. Capacity is 1 crore cases per annum, with 15-20 lakh cases targeted in FY27 at about INR600 per case, roughly INR120 crore revenue at that realisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore (management called INR1,440-1,450 crore quite possible), assuming Bhopal resumes operations.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at close to 10%; FY28 guidance to be given in about six months due to inflation in glass bottles, cans and barley.
Q1 FY27 results expected to be better than Q4 FY26, helped by better utilisation at Hassan and Odisha and some one-off annual costs in Q4 not recurring.
Management expects Bhopal market share to return to earlier levels about six to seven months after the plant restarts.
UP plant expected to start commercial production in June 2026; full capacity ramp-up expected to take 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bhopal plant licence renewal is underway; management said it could be resolved in a couple of weeks, but later said a resolution could come within 7-10 days and gave no definite date.
UP brewery (1 crore cases per annum): trials under way, commercial operations expected from June 2026; Phase 1 is the brewery and no further capex is needed beyond working capital.
About INR400 crore of credit lines sanctioned but not drawn, which management will use only after Bhopal is operational.
Possible Phase 2 of the UP project could be the use of new promoter or warrant funds; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Karnataka (about 30-35% of business) is improving after the state's excise duty rationalisation, which lowered MRP on mainstream and economy beer; management says it is gaining share over the last 3-4 quarters.
Industry volume in April and May 2026 grew about 15-16% combined, with April at 51-52 lakh cases and May at about 50 lakh cases despite rain.
Delhi, Jharkhand and UP supplies from Bhopal have stopped; Jharkhand is partly served from Odisha, while some markets are not cost-effective to serve from other plants.
Andhra Pradesh business expected to start in the next 3-4 weeks; Tamil Nadu share is growing.
Input cost inflation in glass bottles, aluminium cans, barley and logistics is the main margin pressure; long-term supply contracts are not holding price.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA margin outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore, with the Bhopal licence assumed. FY27 EBITDA margin close to 10%; FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the UP plant contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: 15-20 lakh cases from UP in FY27 at roughly INR600 per case, about INR120 crore; plant capacity is 1 crore cases per annum with a 2-3 year ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 going to be as loss-making as Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects Q1 to be better than Q4 on higher Hassan and Odisha utilisation and lower annual costs booked in Q4. Only labour cost at Bhopal will fall; no salary cuts were made.

qa_highlights.question: How long to regain Bhopal and MP market share once the plant reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to recover the similar market share within about six months, though the main season makes it harder now. Management said the sales and distribution team is ready and waiting.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-time impact from Karnataka's excise cut?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-time impact. The MRP cut lowers consumer prices; management said revenue would rise slightly and margins would not suffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the licence lost and what internal steps are being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some matters are sub judice and cannot be discussed. It is appointing a dedicated compliance officer and improving compliance processes. The company said the rating downgrades stem only from the licence suspension.

risks_watch: Bhopal licence renewal timing is open-ended. Management's timelines have slipped from days to weeks to months, and the FY27 guidance depends on it.
Input cost inflation (glass, cans, barley) with no fixed-price contracts; FY28 margin guidance deferred.
Credit rating downgrades at parent and subsidiary; management says ratings will recover once the licence is restored. About INR400 crore of undrawn lines are available.
Governance: the Company Secretary resigned (personal reasons, per management) and an internal auditor left; a compliance officer is being appointed.
Market share loss in MP and Delhi may not be fully recovered, per management's own comments.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid about FY26 being a tough year but was confident in its recovery plan. Answers on the Bhopal licence timeline were evasive and kept changing, and management declined to discuss sub judice matters. Forward statements on Karnataka and UP were more confident.
key_quotes: Management remains confident of a favorable resolution and does not anticipate any long-term impact on the company's operations.
This downgrade in the rating is only due to the temporary suspension of the license. This is not to do with any financial as such.
We are as much worried as you are. I think it's our endeavor to get it solved at the earliest.
